hero.title: History
hero.subtitle: The journey of a city that never stopped reinventing itself.

intro.mainBefore: If you think you've seen it all in a city, it's because you still
intro.p1: In the heart of Minas Gerais' Zona da Mata, the city stands out for its pioneering spirit, vibrant history, and unique ability to reinvent itself.
intro.p2: It was here that Latin America witnessed the first open TV broadcast and where Bernardo Mascarenhas made history with the first hydroelectric power plant dedicated to public lighting on the continent.
intro.p3: At the end of the 19th century, Juiz de Fora earned the title of "Mineira Manchester" thanks to the textile factories that placed the city among the most promising in Brazil.
intro.palaceCaption: Old City Hall — now the Special Office for Racial Equality

quote.mainBefore: Juiz de Fora made it into the record books with the
quote.mainAfter: served at a single event — just a taste of what our Mineira cuisine has to offer.
quote.places: From the Mariano Procópio Museum to the Cine-Theatro Central, passing by the Morro do Imperador viewpoint and Halfeld Park, every corner of the city reveals experiences that blend tradition and innovation.
quote.conclusion: Juiz de Fora is plural, creative, and diverse.

timeline.title: Time
timeline.description: More than three centuries of milestones that turned a settlers' village into one of the most influential cities in the Geraes.

1703.text: Start of the Caminho Novo, linking Minas to Rio and driving the rise of villages such as Santo Antônio do Paraibuna.

1853.text: Santo Antônio do Paraibuna is elevated to city status; European technicians are hired for the União e Indústria Road.

1856.text: Twenty European craftsmen arrive to help build the road.

1857.text: 1,162 German immigrants arrive, forming a colonial nucleus in the region.

1861.text: Visit by Emperor Dom Pedro II; the palace is built by Manoel do Vale Amado.

1865.text: Santo Antônio do Paraibuna is officially renamed Juiz de Fora.

1890.text: Construction of the "Castelinho", headquarters of the Mineira Electricity Company.

1907.text: The Santa Mafalda Palace becomes the First Public School.

1915.text: The Mariano Procópio Museum is founded by Alfredo Ferreira Lage.

1929.text: Inauguration of the Cine-Theatro Central in eclectic architectural style.

1934.text: Founding of the Turunas do Riachuelo samba school.

1977.text: Creation of the Miss Gay Brasil contest, a milestone in LGBTQIAPN+ culture.

2023.text: Reopening of the restored palace; celebration of the city's architectural and cultural history.

origins.p1: Juiz de Fora wasn't born by chance. Its history began around 1703, with the opening of the Caminho Novo, a strategic route between Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro, created to transport gold and oversee tax collection by the Portuguese Crown.
origins.p2: Several settlements emerged along this road, among them Santo Antônio do Paraibuna — which would become one of the pioneer cities of Minas Gerais. In 1853 it was elevated to city status and, twelve years later, received its definitive name: Juiz de Fora.
origins.p3: And yes, there really was a "juiz de fora" (outside judge)! In colonial times, magistrates from other regions were appointed to avoid local favoritism. The expression stuck and ended up naming the city.

immigration.p1: With the city in full development, the construction of the União e Indústria Road, conceived by Mariano Procópio Ferreira Lage, would further drive its growth. Considered one of the first modern highways in Latin America, it connected Juiz de Fora to Petrópolis.
immigration.p2: In 1857, 1,162 German immigrants arrived — a number equivalent to about 20% of the local population. They settled in the present-day neighborhoods of São Pedro, Borboleta, and Fábrica. Over time, they moved into urban life as workers, carpenters, and cart drivers, integrating with the city and the União e Indústria Company.

manchester.imageCaption: Source: Juiz de Fora City Hall
manchester.p1: Juiz de Fora earned the title of "Mineira Manchester" at the end of the 19th century, in reference to the English city symbol of the Industrial Revolution. The nickname reflected its important role in the industrial development of Minas Gerais, driven by the textile industries.
manchester.p2: Bernardo Mascarenhas, a visionary entrepreneur, founded the Mineira Electricity Company in 1888 and built the Marmelos Power Plant — the first in Latin America to provide electric power for public lighting.
manchester.p3: The old Textile Factory building was revitalized and today is part of the Mascarenhas Complex, where tradition and innovation meet at the Bernardo Mascarenhas Cultural Center and the Municipal Market — reopened in 2025.

architecture.p1: Walking through the streets of Juiz de Fora is like flipping through a memoir. The Santa Mafalda Palace, built in the 1850s as a gift to Emperor Dom Pedro II, was turned into a school and restored in 2023.
architecture.p2: The "Castelinho", erected in 1890, impresses with its medieval architecture. Alfredo Ferreira Lage transformed his family's villa into the Mariano Procópio Museum. French landscaper Auguste Glaziou brought the charm of English gardens to the park.
architecture.p3: Even Cândido Portinari left his mark with two public panels on the façade of the Edifício Clube Juiz de Fora. And the Cine-Theatro Central, inaugurated in 1929, continues to host great performances.

surprise.p1: At Carnival, the city carries memories that mix African rhythms and Carioca influences. It was here that, in 1934, the Turunas do Riachuelo was born — the first samba school in Minas Gerais and the fourth in Brazil.
surprise.p2: Since 1977, Juiz de Fora has hosted Miss Brasil Gay, a milestone for LGBTQIAPN+ culture in the country. With its colors, performances, and celebration of plurality, the event has become a symbol of respect and inclusion.
surprise.tagline: Get ready to be surprised on every visit.
